title: Micro PRD One‑pager — Snippet Synthesizer (wildnotes)
content:
Context / intuition:
- I keep losing time writing changelogs + release notes for small infra/model updates. repetitive, low-value for humans but useful for customers and internal comms.
- Goal: let teams generate short, high-signal snippet summaries from commit messages, PR titles, and eval diffs via Redwood hosted inference. reduce manual drafting and standardize tone.

Product idea (one line):
- Snippet Synthesizer: a lightweight endpoint + console flow that takes a compact input bundle (commits, PR description, changed files, perf delta) and emits 1–3 short, structured release snippets (one-line changelog, 2‑sentence user-facing blurb, internal impact note).

Why Redwood?
- Fits a hosted API use case (fast adoption).
- Opportunity to show cost controls: tiny response sizes, strict token caps, batching for bursts.
- Useful demo for streaming / structured output features in console.

Key user stories (MVP):
1) As an engineer, I can POST a small JSON with PR title + commit msgs + perf delta and get back a one-line changelog in a consistent tone.
2) As a PM, I can request a user-facing blurb and an internal impact note (2 outputs) in one call and choose tone=helpful|concise|marketing.
3) As a platform integrator, I can configure a per-team token cap and auto-batch daily PRs to save cost.
4) As a docs writer, I can mark a generated snippet as "approved" in the console and store it to the org snippets bucket.

MVP acceptance criteria (practical):
- Endpoint returns JSON with exactly three fields: changelog_line, user_blurb, internal_note. no extra prose.
- Each output respects token limits (<= 40 tokens for changelog_line, <= 80 for user_blurb).
- True positive rate: on a small hand-labeled set of 250 PRs, generated changelog_line judged acceptable by human editors >= 75%.
- Cost-per-generation target: < $0.002 (hosted) at median with 90th percentile < $0.01.

Non-goals for MVP:
- Do not try to infer stakeholder names or map to product-side release channels yet.
- Not building long-form release notes generator. keep single-shot micro summaries.

Open questions / risks (quick list):
- Safety: leaked sensitive token in commit diffs? Need to strip secrets automatically. include preflight scrubber.
- Data residency: some customers may want Private for release notes that reference internal bug numbers. MVP stays hosted.
- Eval signal: what metrics to track in Console? human accept rate, edit distance to final accepted blurb, token usage, latency.
- Batching: should backend batch by team each 30s window? or provide explicit batch API?

Technical sketch (very rough):
- API: /v1/snippets/generate (POST). Accepts: input_items: [(pr_title, commits[], perf_delta_optional, diff_stats)], tone, team_id, max_tokens_hint.
- Runtime: prefer small open model (quantized) with short-context optimizations. use KV caching for repeated repo boilerplate (license headers, common PR templates) to shave tokens.
- Cost controls: token_budget per-team + hard token cutoff enforced at runtime; default 60 tokens total.
- Batching: worker queues group by team_id for 100ms micro-batches; optional scheduled daily-batch mode where client uploads multiple PRs and receives zips.
- Output format: strict JSON schema; if model hallucinated extra fields, server truncates/normalizes.

Console + UX notes:
- Small table view: PRs | generated snippet | accept/replace | version history | token usage per generate.
- Quick keyboard shortcut to accept and copy to clipboard.
- Toggle model variant (fast/cheap vs higher-fidelity) with estimated cost preview.

Experiment plan / small eval:
- Build classifier/eval harness: sample 300 PRs across infra, SDK, docs. Generate snippets with two model sizes and two prompting templates. Human labelers mark accept/reject + minor_edit_required.
- Measure cost, latency, and accept rate. Pick default config that hits accept >=75% and p50 latency < 400ms.

Metrics dashboard (Console):
- Generated per team/day, accepted_rate, median_tokens, cost-per-gen, 95p latency, hallucination_rate (human label), scrub_failure_rate (secrets found).

Implementation TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Proto API + type defs and example curl payloads (Victor to own).
- [ ] Prompt templates + baseline eval harness (Maya).
- [ ] Simple scrubber pipeline (remove long hex strings, emails, API keys) (Luca).
- [ ] Console mock: list view and quick accept action (design sprint).

Notes to self / stylistic experiments:
- Try both "imperative" prompts (write a short changelog) and "extractive" prompts (summarize the PR title into one sentence) — extractive might reduce hallucination.
- Consider a tiny retrieval step: repo README or PR template as context to increase alignment. cache per-repo.

Misc (bonsai note):
- Keep this feature trimmed: tiny, repeatable, easy to approve. like a bonsai — short, shaped, high signal.

Immediate next step: wire a PR-level demo that takes last 10 merged PRs from a test repo and generates snippets. If that looks good, open a small alpha cohort in infra.

Random parking-lot ideas (not for MVP):
- Auto-rollout notes: generate A/B test descriptions for feature flags.
- Multi-lingual changelogs.
- Auto-tagging to sections (bugfix, perf, docs).

-- tori
